steps.scene: You're driving along a line of parked cars near a park. A football bounces out into the road ahead of you.

options.text: Slow right down and be ready to stop for a child
Hold your speed and sound the horn as a warning
Stop and wave whoever comes out across the road

question.explanation: Where a ball goes, a child follows — and they won't be looking. Cover the brake before you see them.

steps.title: School crossing patrol
steps.body: A patrol steps into the road holding a 'stop' sign. You must stop, and stay stopped until they and the children are clear of the road.

question.prompt: A school crossing patrol steps out ahead of you. What will they hold up?

options.text: An arm, raised from the kerb
A 'stop' sign
A red light on a pole

question.explanation: The 'stop' sign is an order, not a request. Wait — and never wave children across yourself.

question.prompt: Amber lights are flashing under this sign. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to clear the area before the children reach it
Wait at the lights until they stop flashing
Cut your speed until you're clear of the area

question.explanation: The lights are switched on when children may be crossing. Slow down and be ready to stop.

steps.title: Yellow zigzags outside a school
steps.body: Don't wait or park on them, even for a moment. A parked car hides the school entrance and hides the children stepping out of it.

question.prompt: What do the yellow zigzag lines outside a school mean?

options.text: You may stop on them to drop off or pick up children
You should not wait or park your vehicle here
You may park here if you stay with the vehicle

question.explanation: The markings keep the view of the school entrance clear, both for drivers and for the children crossing.

steps.wrongBelief: If the mirrors look clear behind you, it's safe to start reversing.

question.prompt: You can't be sure the area behind your car is clear. What should you do?

options.text: Check the mirrors again and reverse slowly
Get out and check before you move
Carry on, assuming it's clear behind you

question.explanation: Mirrors leave a blind area right behind the car. If you cannot tell, the only safe check is on foot.

steps.repairNote: Mirrors don't see everything. Where there might be children or a low obstruction, get out and look before you reverse.

steps.title: Who disappears behind your car
steps.body: A small child can stand right behind your boot and be invisible through the rear window. They're the road users you're least likely to see.

question.prompt: Which road users are hardest to see while you're reversing?

options.text: Children
Motorcyclists
Car drivers behind you

question.explanation: Anyone short enough to sit below the rear window vanishes. Check on foot when children may be about.

steps.scene: You're about to reverse into a side road. Someone is standing on the kerb waiting to cross behind your car.

options.text: Reverse before they start to cross
Give way and let them cross first
Sound your horn to warn them you're reversing

question.explanation: Stop and let anyone waiting cross behind you. Don't wave or signal them past — you can't see the whole road.
